Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:1.hebrew: מדקתני סיפא - כחס על הנר כו' חייב חטאת, אם שגג בשבת — ששכח שהוא שבת, או סבר שכיבוי מותר בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:1.english: From the fact that the latter clause teaches - "[If one acted] to spare the lamp," etc., "he is liable" — [meaning liable to bring] a sin-offering, if he acted unwittingly on Shabbat, [in] that he forgot that it was Shabbat, or thought that extinguishing [a flame] is permitted on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:2.hebrew: ש"מ ר' יהודה היא - דאמר: מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה — חייב עליה. דכיבוי זה אין צריך לגופו, אלא לצורך דבר אחר: שלא תדלק הפתילה, או שלא יפקע הנר. ואין לך כיבוי הצריך לגופו אלא כיבוי של פחמין כשעושין אותו, וכיבוי של הבהוב פתילה, שהכיבוי נעשה להאחיז בו האור מהר כשירצה להדליקו. וכיון דרבי יהודה היא, רישא דפטר משום חולה — וה"ה לשאר פטורי דמתניתין:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:2.english: Conclude from it [that] it is Rabbi Yehuda - For he said: [One who performs] a labor not needed for its own sake is liable for it. For this extinguishing is not needed for its own sake, but rather for the sake of something else: so that the wick does not burn [away], or so that the lamp does not crack. And you have no extinguishing that is needed for its own sake other than the extinguishing of charcoals when they make them, and the extinguishing of singeing a wick, where the extinguishing is done to make the fire catch on it quickly when one wishes to light it. And since it is [according to] Rabbi Yehuda, [the Gemara asks regarding] the first clause, which exempts [one who extinguishes] on account of a sick person — and the same applies to the other exemptions of the Mishnah:

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:3.hebrew: אי - דאית בהו סכנת נפשות, ומשום פקוח נפש שרי להו — ליתני מותר לכתחלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:3.english: If - That there is danger to life in them, and because of the saving of life it is permitted for them, let [the mishna] teach [that it is] permitted ab initio.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:4.hebrew: חייב מיבעי ליה - הואיל ורבי יהודה היא, דלא פטר ליה משום דאינה צריכה לגופה:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:1:4.english: It should have [said] liable - Since it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda, who does not exempt him on the grounds that [it is a labor] not needed for its own sake.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:2:1.hebrew: והא דתני רבי אושעיא - בהדיא: ״אבל אסור״:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:2:1.english: And that which Rabbi Oshaya taught - [It states] explicitly: "But it is prohibited."

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:2:2.english: And it is [according to] Rabbi Shimon - For he exempts him because [it is a labor] not needed for its own sake.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:1.english: A question was asked - They asked a question.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:2.hebrew: לעילא מר' תנחום - לפניו. וכן לשון הש"ס והמקרא: ״שרפים עומדים ממעל לו״ (ישעיהו ו׳:ב׳) — ועל שם שיראים להתקרב לפניו, עומדין מרחוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:2.english: Above Rabbi Tanḥum - Before him. And such is the phrasing of the Talmud and Scripture: “Seraphim stood above Him” (Isaiah 6:2) — and because they are afraid to approach before Him, they stand from afar.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:3.english: From Noy - [This is the name of a] place.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:4.hebrew: באישא - חולה; תרגום של רעה — בישתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:4.english: A sick person - [Means] an ill person; the [Aramaic] translation of [the Hebrew word] ra’ah [evil] is bishta.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:5.hebrew: פתח ואמר - כך היו רגילין לפתוח באגדה תחילה, והוא דומה לשאלה, ודרש:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:5.english: He opened and said - Such was their custom, to open with aggadah first — and it was similar to the question — and he expounded:

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:6.english: And then again you said - To contradict your own words.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:7.hebrew: כי לכלב חי - כלומר, גדולים החיים ופקוח נפש:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:7.english: For a living dog - That is to say, life and the saving of life are great.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:3:8.english: Where is it - Where has it gone?

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:4:1.english: [This is] not difficult - He himself [Rabbi Tanḥum] was explaining them:

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:4:2.english: That which Rabbi Yoḥanan said - He was expounding a verse: “Set free among the dead.”

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:1.hebrew: ושבח אני את המתים - שעסקו בחייהם בתורה ומצות ומתו, ראויים לשבחם אפילו מצדיקים חיים, שגדולים הן במיתתן מבחייהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:1.english: And I praised the dead - [Those] who engaged in Torah and mitzvot during their lifetime and died are worthy of being praised even [more than] living righteous people, for they are greater in their death than in their lifetime.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:2.hebrew: עמד משה - ואין לך צדיק ממנו, ולא נענה בזכותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:2.english: Moses stood - And you have no one more righteous than him, yet he was not answered in his [own] merit.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:3.hebrew: ותקן כמה תקנות - כי ההיא דתני במגילה (דף ד. ולב.), משה תיקן להם לישראל שיהו שואלין ודורשין בעניינו של יום:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:5:3.english: And instituted several ordinances - Like that which is taught in Megillah (daf 4a and 32a): Moses instituted for Israel that they should inquire and expound on the matter of the day.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:6:1.hebrew: ד"א ושבח אני את המתים - הראשונים, מן החיים של עכשיו — שהראשונים טובים מאלה. תדע, שמתקיימות גזרותיו של משה, ואין מתקיימות גזירות שרים של עכשיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:6:1.english: Another explanation: “And I praised the dead” - [This refers to] the earlier [generations], more than the living of today — for the earlier ones are better than these. You may know [this], for the decrees of Moses are fulfilled, while the decrees of contemporary ministers are not fulfilled.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:6:2.english: For that sin - [The sin] of Bathsheba.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:1.english: The gates clung [together] - [The gates] of the Holy of Holies.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:2.hebrew: כ"ד רננות - רנה, תפילה, תחינה כתובים בתפילת שלמה עד כ"ד. ויש אומרים: כ"ד ברכות דתענית, ולא נהירא:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:2.english: Twenty-four songs of praise - [The words] 'song,' 'prayer,' [and] 'supplication' are written in Solomon’s prayer up to twenty-four [times]. And some say [it refers to] the twenty-four blessings of a fast day, but this does not seem correct.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:3.hebrew: רהטו שערים בתריה למבלעיה - סברי דעל עצמו אמר "מלך הכבוד". א"ל שערים: "מי הוא זה מלך הכבוד?". אמר איהו: "ה' עזוז וגבור" (תהילים כ״ד:י׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:3.english: The gates ran after him to swallow him - They thought that he said "the King of glory" about himself. The gates said to him: "Who is this King of glory?" He said: "The Lord strong and mighty" (Psalms 24:10).

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:4.hebrew: שונאי דוד - משפחת שאול, שמעי, וכיוצא בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:7:4.english: David’s enemies - The family of Saul, Shimei, and those like him.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:8:1.hebrew: דיום הכפורים - שאכלו ושתו בחנוכת הבית, כדכתיב: ״את החג שבעת ימים ושבעת ימים״, כדאמרינן במועד קטן (דף ט.):
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:8:1.english: [The sin] of Yom Kippur - That they ate and drank at the dedication of the Temple, as it is written: “the feast, seven days and seven days” (I Kings 8:65), as we say in Moed Katan (9a).

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:1.hebrew: ודקאמר שלמה כי לכלב חי הוא טוב מאריה המת - לאו לענין חשיבותא אמרו, אלא לענין הלכות שבת וי"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:1.english: And that which Solomon said: “For a living dog is better than a dead lion” - He did not say it with regard to importance, but rather with regard to the laws of Shabbat and Yom Tov.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:2.english: My end - The [events] destined to come upon me.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:3.english: The measure of my days - How many the days of my life [are].

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:4.english: How short-lived I am - On which day I will cease and depart from the world.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:5.english: Let me die on the first day of the week - So that they will be able to attend to me and to my eulogy.

Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:6.hebrew: כי טוב יום בחצריך - כלומר, כבר אמרת לפני: ״טוב יום שאתה עומד בחצרי ועוסק בתורה מאלף עולות שעתיד בנך שלמה להעלות״, כדכתיב (מלכים א ג) ״אלף עולות יעלה שלמה וגו'״:
Rashi on Shabbat 30a:9:6.english: For a day in Your courts is better - That is to say, you have already said previously: “A day that you stand in My courts and engage in Torah is better than a thousand burnt-offerings that your son Solomon is destined to offer up,” as it is written (I Kings 3): “A thousand burnt-offerings did Solomon offer,” etc.
